title: Fried Cheese Burekas with Honey
subtitle: with a rose and basil seed yoghurt dip
description: Fried half-moons of a cooked-flour dough filled with ricotta, mozzarella, pecorino and parmesan, drizzled with lavender honey and served with a rose and basil seed yoghurt dip.

steps.text: Bring 250 ml water and the olive oil to the boil, reduce to medium-low, add 90 g of the 00 flour, the durum flour and 1 tsp of the salt, and cook for 5 minutes, stirring vigorously. Remove from the heat, cool slightly, shape into a ball by hand, wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Mix the cooked dough in a mixer with a dough hook for 30 seconds. Add 1 egg yolk and 400 g of 00 flour and mix until you have a stable dough.
Roll out to 2 mm thick with a pasta machine or rolling pin and cut 10 cm rounds. The dough can be made up to 3 days ahead; take it out of the fridge 20 minutes before rolling.
Whisk the remaining 2 egg yolks and the egg, crumble in the ricotta, add the mozzarella, pecorino, parmesan, mint and 4 g salt and mix until even.
Place a spoonful of filling on each round, brush the edges with a little water, fold into half-moons and press to seal.
Heat oil for deep frying in a wide, deep pot. Fry 2-3 burekas at a time, about 1 1/2 minutes per side, turning with a slotted spoon. Drain on a plate.
Meanwhile, bring the honey, 2 tablespoons water and the lavender to the boil for about 1 minute and remove from the heat.
Mix the yoghurt, 50 ml water, basil seeds, rose petals and rosewater and leave for 20 minutes until the seeds swell and the dip thickens slightly.
Arrange the burekas on a platter, pour the honey over, scatter with blue cheese if using, and serve with the yoghurt dip.
